answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that is slashed on double-signing. A Sybil farmer must fund one bond per fake voice, and each can only whisper as loudly as its stake permits, so scale costs real capital. Verified peers form an oasis of trusted routes, while unbonded copies earn no fees and wear no saffron badge. Impersonation therefore costs the full collateral plus lost yield, exceeding any gain.
